subject: Science
title: Researching the Solar System
objective_verbatim: Research and present findings about the Solar System (ICT).
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 3.73 on 824 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 9.73 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: check a source and share a fact about the Solar System.
success_criteria: I can find a fact on a class source card.
I can name the card that supports my fact.
I can fix a claim that the card does not support.

vocab.definition: the Sun and the objects that move around it
vocab.example: Earth is part of our Solar System.

vocab.definition: a large, nearly round body that moves around a star
vocab.example: Earth is a planet that moves around the Sun.

vocab.definition: a hot body in space that makes its own light
where a fact or idea comes from

retrieval.question: What shape is the Moon roughly?
Why do we get day and night?

stages.pupil_text: Choose the body that makes its own light: Sun, Earth or Moon.
stages.adult_text: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question.
stages.adult_text: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

stages.pupil_text: I read card B: Earth goes round the Sun. I point to card B as my source. A claim without a matching source is a guess.
stages.adult_text: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

stages.pupil_text: Card A is matched to Sun is a star. Card B has a fact but no label. Find the missing source label for Earth goes round the Sun.
stages.adult_text: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: Choose the claim that our class fact cards support. Show one answer at the same time.
stages.adult_text: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

stages.pupil_text: Share two facts about the Solar System. Name the class card that supports each fact. Correct one claim if its card does not match.
stages.adult_text: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: Hear which card backs your fact. Change a source label or fact if needed, then say what changed.
stages.adult_text: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).

stages.pupil_text: Say one checked fact and point to the matching class card. Say which source label you fixed.
stages.adult_text: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

worked_example.full: Claim: Earth goes round the Sun → card B says the same → cite card B.
worked_example.faded: Claim: The Moon goes round Earth → card C says the same → cite card ____.
worked_example.removed_step: Choose and name the source card for the Moon claim.
worked_example.fade_next: Next time omit the ready claim and ask the pupil to choose a claim from two cards.

cfu.question: Card B says Earth goes round the Sun. Which card should I name with that claim?

hinge.question: Which claim is backed by our class cards?

options.diagnosis: Confuses a planet with a star.
Confuses a natural satellite with a planet.

options.text: Card C says Earth goes round the Sun.
options.diagnosis: Chooses the wrong source label even for a true fact.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on. Otherwise re-model with the named I-do example, then ask the parallel hinge.
hinge.parallel_hinge: Which card backs ‘The Moon goes round Earth’: A, B or C? Answer: C.

misconceptions.misconception: Earth makes its own light like a star.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses A, “Earth makes its own light.”
misconceptions.correction: Use card A for the Sun as a star; Earth is a planet that receives light.

misconceptions.misconception: Any card can support a true claim.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses D, which names card C for an orbit claim not on that card.
misconceptions.correction: Match the actual wording of the claim with card B.

we_do.H: Explain why card A supports the Sun claim but does not support the Moon claim.

tiers.F: Point to one fact and its source card.
tiers.M: Share two facts and name each matching card.
tiers.H: Use two cards to explain Earth’s place, then repair a false label.

stems.M: My fact is ___; card ___ supports it.
stems.H: Card ___ supports ___, but it cannot show ___ because ___.

tiers.go_deeper: A poster calls the Moon a planet. Use two class cards to repair the label and name both sources.
tiers.early_finisher: Two cards disagree about the Moon. Choose the supported claim, then name a reliable source for a further check.

stages: Arrival (5 min): Choose the body that makes its own light: Sun, Earth or Moon. Staff: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question. Staff: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

I Do (5 min): I read card B: Earth goes round the Sun. I point to card B as my source. A claim without a matching source is a guess. Staff: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

We Do (7 min): Card A is matched to Sun is a star. Card B has a fact but no label. Find the missing source label for Earth goes round the Sun. Staff: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.
We Do 2 (5 min): Choose the claim that our class fact cards support. Show one answer at the same time. Staff: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

Independent (8 min): Share two facts about the Solar System. Name the class card that supports each fact. Correct one claim if its card does not match. Staff: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.

Review (4 min): Hear which card backs your fact. Change a source label or fact if needed, then say what changed. Staff: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).

Exit (3 min): Say one checked fact and point to the matching class card. Say which source label you fixed. Staff: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

if_behind.must_teach_core: Share two facts about the Solar System. Name the class card that supports each fact. Correct one claim if its card does not match. Preserve the individual evidence required above.
if_behind.shorten_or_merge: After a secure hinge, shorten repeated oral rehearsal. If needed, merge the exit reflection into the Arrival of Autumn 2 W04. Keep the core evidence and any safety teaching; record the change and coverage impact.

if_behind.dependency: Pass on today’s checked understanding and unresolved hinge errors for the next starter. Do not replace incomplete individual work with a group product.
